collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — ADVICE AND DECISIONS (ADV-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Asking for advice, giving it, ignoring it, following half of it, and deciding alone. Advice can be wrong, even from elders and experts. Following it doesn't guarantee a good outcome and ignoring it doesn't cause a bad one. Feeling heard with no decision is a perfectly good ending, and nobody ever has to admit someone else was right.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

collection.description: A master carver tells an apprentice the fish's tail is too thick: say they do not want to hear it now, or listen anyway.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) looks at (friend)'s carving and says, kindly but plainly, "The fish is good, but the tail's too thick, and you've rushed the eye." (friend)'s face goes hot. (friend.He/she) worked on that carving for three days. (friend.He/she) doesn't want to hear about the tail.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: "I don't want to hear it right now," says (friend), a little sharply. (subject) nods. "Fair enough. It'll keep." (friend) goes home, puts the carving on a shelf and glares at it for a week. Then one evening (friend.he/she) picks it up, looks at the tail and thinks: too thick. And the eye. Rushed. (friend.He/she) never tells (subject). (friend.He/she) just carves the next one better.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (friend) swallows (friend.his/her) pride and listens. It's not easy. (subject) shows (friend.him/her) how to thin a tail with long, light strokes. (friend) tries it. It's a little better. (friend.He/she) still thinks (friend.his/her) original eye was fine, and says so. "Then keep the eye," says (subject). "It's your fish." (friend) keeps the eye.
